correctness.summary: The non-Euclidean Heron-L'Huilier formulas reduce fixed-perimeter/fixed-deficit area optimization to transformed products in the complementary semiperimeter variables. A divided-difference argument shows these products are strictly increasing in xyz at fixed first two moments, so the explicit two-equal-variable extrema and the D/p^2=1/8 boundary contact give the claimed sharp profiles.

limitations: The spherical theorem is restricted to geodesically convex minor-arc triangles with perimeter below 2π.
Curvature is normalized to ±1; other radii follow by scaling.
Only the Finsler-Hadwiger side deficit is optimized.
The Euclidean specialization is prior work and is included only as a consistency check.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge; equivalent transformed-variable formulations in older literature remain a residual risk.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Svrtan-Veljan provide non-Euclidean Finsler-Hadwiger and isoperimetric inequalities, while Bogosel gives the complete sharp Euclidean area/perimeter/deficit diagram. No checked source gives the corresponding complete spherical or hyperbolic fixed-perimeter/fixed-deficit area profiles, equality families, and lower-envelope phase transition.

value.summary: The result connects the established non-Euclidean Finsler-Hadwiger program with the modern complete Euclidean diagram, producing exact sharp area intervals rather than a single one-sided inequality in both curvature signs.
